title: Engineering Biological-Based Vascular Grafts Using a Pulsatile Bioreactor
protocol: Autoclave the tubing for the flow system and bioreactor components.
Assemble the bioreactor itself and the silicone stopper lid as instructed.
Cut PGA mesh to a size of 1.1cm x ~8cm sheet.
Clean silicone tubing (3mm inner diameter) with distilled water and air dry before usage.
Use Dexon 6.0 suture to sew PGA mesh around the clean silicone tubing starting with three surgical knots followed by single stitches.
Dip PGA scaffolds in 1M NaOH for 1-2 minutes.
Rinse PGA scaffolds in distilled water baths for 2 minutes, repeating this process three times.
Pat PGA scaffolds dry with Kimwipes between each dip in distilled water baths.
Dry PGA scaffolds under a tissue culture hood to air dry for 15 minutes with blower on.
Use Prolene 4.0 suture to sew small pieces of Dacron cuffs (1cm) onto each end of the PGA mesh with an overlap of 2-3mm.
Ensure not to puncture silicone tubing during sewing.
Sew three stitches around the free end of Dacron cuffs using the same suture.
Leave enough sutures at the free ends of Prolene suture for step 5.1.
Assemble the bioreactor components on the day before beginning bioreactor culture.
Soak sewn mesh, silicone tubing, surgical instruments, and a thin wire in a 70% ethanol bath for 20-30 minutes.
Submerge the bioreactor from autoclave pouches into the 70% ethanol bath for at least 30 minutes.
Flush the bioreactor thoroughly with ethanol.
Pull silicone tubing through side-arms using a thin wire.
Take the bioreactor out of the ethanol bath, keeping the mesh submerged in ethanol.
Fix the PGA scaffold inside the bioreactor by tightening and tying down Prolene sutures over Dacron cuffs on flared glass lips.
Connect one side of the bioreactor's side arms to connectors via silicone tubing.
Pull the other side of the silicone tubing with tension and insert the remaining two connectors into the silicone tubing.
Reinsert the bioreactor into the ethanol bath, flush with ethanol by gently pulling connectors out of the side arms.
Flip the bioreactor over and allow a soak for 10 minutes.
Flip the bioreactor right-side up and soak for an additional 10 minutes.
Drain all ethanol from the bioreactor.
Set up three large petri dishes (10 cm) in series.
Place the bioreactor in the center dish to hold excess ethanol dripped from tube ends.
Flush bioreactor and PGA mesh with tissue culture water using a 5ml or 10ml pipette.
Flush tissue culture water into silicone tubing.
Thoroughly drain all excess water into petri dishes on either side of the bioreactor.
Dry bioreactor overnight in hood with blower on and UV OFF.
Place a sterile petri dish over opening of each bioreactor to protect the PGA scaffold inside from contaminants.
Assemble flow system to bioreactor as indicated.
Parafilm all connection joints.
Wipe connectors first with alcohol wipes.
Attach injection port to third, unused arm of bioreactor.
Remove walrus tubing and tie off blue end of saline dilution set as close to Y-junction as possible.
Pull tube clamp in place to ensure no liquid transfer to this part of the tube.
Remove IV bag and attach walrus tubing (red) to far end of IV bag.
Wipe insertion port with alcohol wipe first.
Attach walrus to one side of flow system (via white end tube).
Insert 3-way stopcock into flow system.
Remove pressure transducer and connect to three-way stopcock.
Attach other end of pressure transducer to middle opening in bag.
Connect the bioreactor to the flow system via the Y-junction.
Mix 5 ml fungizone with 495 ml PBS to prepare a 1% fungizone solution.
Add 350 ml of 1% fungizone solution to an IV bag using a 60 ml syringe.
Squeeze the IV bag to flush the flow system by adjusting stop cocks.
Resuspend 8 x 10^6 SMCs in 1.25 ml of medium and seed onto each PGA scaffold.
Ensure cell suspension is uniformly dripped onto the PGA mesh-Dacron junction and bottom side of PGA mesh.
Wipe rim of bioreactor with alcohol wipe by rotating the bioreactor sideways.
Attach injection port to feeding tube at male connector.
Attach PTFE 0.20 μm filters to each air port.
Parafilm the injection port.
Insert silicone stopper lid into glass bioreactor ensuring feeding tube does not touch seeded PGA scaffolds.
Parafilm around the lid.
Place bioreactor with flow system inside incubator on its side.
Rotate bioreactor every 5 minutes for 25-30 minutes.
Fill bioreactor chamber with 400 ml of optimized culture medium.
Grow seeded scaffolds statically without pulsatile pumping through silicone tubing for 6-7 days.
Check for leaks of PBS or kinking of flow system tubing before turning on the pump.
Turn on the pump and adjust settings to maintain a pressure reading of approximately 270/-30mmHg.
Record pressures daily throughout culture and ensure maintenance at 270/-30mmHg.
Assemble injection port & PTFE filter onto feeding lids for medium change and waste disposal purposes.
Place the feeding tube firmly on the pump, inserting one end to the bioreactor's feeding port and the other to the feeding lid.
Wipe injection ports with ethanol wipes.
Pump out 200ml of medium using a dual-directional Masterflex pump.
Insert a new feeding tube to pump 200ml of fresh medium back into the bioreactor.
Start pumping medium at a very slow speed, especially when returning it to the bioreactor.
Change medium and supplement ascorbic acid 2x/week.
Use a 30ml syringe to remove 25ml of medium from the culture.
Place removed medium aside in the tissue hood.
Dissolve 25mg of ascorbic acid in 5ml of PBS.
Filter the dissolved ascorbic acid through a 0.22 μm filter.
Inject sterile ascorbic acid solution into the feeding tube.
Add back the previously removed 25ml medium to the culture.
Mix CuSO4 at a concentration of 1.5 μg in 1 ml PBS.
Dilute Penicillin G to a concentration of 10,000 units/ml.
Prepare PDGF-BB solution at a concentration of 10 ng/ml.
Prepare bFGF solution at a concentration of 10 ng/ml.
Filter all components except PDGF-BB and bFGF through a 0.2 μm filter prior to use.
